#2678. 2026 Big Ten Roundup Week 11-- UCLA stay undefeated, Indiana beats USC

The 2026 college football regular season has almost concluded and to round out Week 11, the Big Ten Conference played a full nine games.

The Big Ten Conference has continued to battle one another, but this week, there weren't too many shocking outcomes. UCLA and Indiana stayed ahead of the rest of the conference in the standings. Here were the outcomes of the nine conference matchups.

It was a rainy, messy game at the Rose Bowl Stadium, but the Bruins found a way to pull out the win in a way to make Hollywood proud. The Bruins senior signal caller Ty Dieffenbach was injured just before half time, but he returned to the field to the sound of roaring applause and delivered a touchdown drive to begin the fourth quarter. Of course, the Bruins defense aided their win with three-turnovers and a safety. UCLA has proven they are for real and they continue to march towards a College Football Playoff berth.

The Hoosiers and Trojans were in a heavyweight fight with both teams evenly matched in the first half. The second half of the game was a different story though. Indiana took off the gloves and knocked USC out of the game. The Hoosiers defense limited the Trojans to just a field and secured two interceptions in the fourth quarter with Indiana's offense piling up 17-points for the win.

The Boilermakers had trouble getting anything going against the Hawkeyes' menacing defense, which allowed Iowa to continue to rack up the points. In fact, just about every time Iowa had possession, they had a chance to score with just one punt and three missed field goals being the only time the Hawkeyes left the field empty-handed.

The Ducks were in full control of the game against the Wolverines. Whether it was Oregon's junior quarterback Dylan Raiola throwing for 341 yards and four touchdowns or the defense allowing less than 100 passing yards, Michigan stood no chance against the Ducks wielding a buzzsaw.

The Buckeyes avoided disaster with a win at home against the Wildcats, despite the team turning the ball over three times. The Wildcats were unable to capitalize on all of the Buckeyes' errors with just two field goals in the first half and a pair of touchdowns in the final half. Ohio State has a lot to figure out before the season ends, but they were able to stop their losing streak from getting to three.

The Terrapins narrowly defended the SECU Stadium against the Badgers, giving Maryland their second conference win of the season. Maryland scored 10 points in the fourth quarter with the game-winning field goal coming off of Wisconsin's third turnover of the game.

The Cornhuskers didn't make the game easy for the Scarlet Knights with Nebraska's defense obstructing any chance at Rutgers putting up points. Rutgers had just 143 total yards of offense with two second half interceptions to cap off the horrendous day of offensive production. The win ends a four-game losing streak for Nebraska.

Points weren't easy to come by in the second half of the Huskies-Spartans game. Both teams scored a pair of touchdowns in the first half, but then the defenses stepped up. Neither team was able to cross the goal line thanks to defenses stifling offensive possessions and forcing turnovers. It wasn't until the final minutes when Washington was able to break the tie with a one-yard rushing touchdown by senior running back Jayden Limar crossing into the end zone for the win.

The Golden Gophers offense was more or less stagnant with their only points against the Nittany Lions coming in the third quarter. Meanwhile, the Nittany Lions eviscerated Minnesota's defense with 28 first half points and two more touchdowns in the final two quarters. Penn State could do no wrong on offense with four passing touchdowns and two rushing touchdowns with 351 total yards of offense.

#2677. Observations after Brown-Maxey duo scores 58 points in Sixers' win without Embiid

Observations after Brown-Maxey duo scores 58 points in Sixers' win without Embiid originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Jaylen Brown-Tyrese Maxey duo starred, LeBron James reached another milestone, and the Sixers earned a win without Joel Embiid on Sunday afternoon.

They improved to 11-3 on the season with a 131-124 victory over the Pacers at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

Brown scored 31 points and Maxey posted 27.

LeBron James had 15 points and 11 assists. He passed Jason Kidd on Sunday for third in NBA history with 12,092 assists.

Pascal Siakam scored 31 points for the 5-9 Pacers.

On the first day of a back-to-back, the Sixers were down Embiid (right foot plantar fascia injury management), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction), Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The Pacers' injured players included Tyrese Haliburton and Andrew Nembhard.

The Sixers will face the Nets on Monday night in Brooklyn. Here are observations on their win over the Pacers:

Jabari Walker started for the first time this season, opening the game at center. He's been in the Sixers' rotation the past five games since Bona's injury.

Walker set up the Sixers' first basket, swiping a steal and then tossing the ball ahead to Maxey for a fast-break dunk. Maxey and Brown both began well and combined to score all of the Sixers' first 15 points.

Though he conceded five inches to 7-foot Pacers center Ivica Zubac, Walker was solid in his first stint. He got an early post stop on Zubac and then snatched a strong defensive rebound.

Dean Wade was next up for the Sixers at the five. He sunk a three-pointer on his first shot to give the team a 20-16 lead.

Walker ended up playing 25 minutes and posting 11 points and seven rebounds. Going back to the preseason, his stock has steadily risen.

"Here we are again after another game saying Jabari played very well," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "He plays hard, he rebounds, he's got another level of confidence with his shooting this year.

"It's kind of wash, rinse and repeat again with him (today). He was great. … Jabari went in there and battled (Zubac). I thought he certainly matched him, if not outplayed him, which is a heck of a job."

Wade had 12 points and seven boards in 35 minutes. Overall, the Sixers' lack of healthy conventional centers is still a clear deficiency. Of course, everything should be simpler once Embiid is back in action.

The Sixers' defense did not have a sparkling start. The Pacers tallied 35 points in the first quarter and shot 62.5 percent from the field.

Brown helped the Sixers avoid a substantial deficit by draining all sorts of jumpers. He rarely appears bothered by close contests. Brown moved to 7 for 9 from the floor when he knocked down a three early in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope's triple knotted the contest up at 37-all.

Nurse needed to stray from his Plan A rotation when VJ Edgecombe picked up his third foul with 9:56 left in the second quarter. Labaron Philon Jr., who got a game with the G League's Delaware Blue Coats on Friday night, subbed in.

For a rookie guard, Philon has looked comfortable and confident on offense in most of his NBA appearances. He swished a long-range jumper in the second quarter and saw a floater rim out.

Brown reached the 20-point mark and put the Sixers up one with a slam assisted by James late in the second quarter.

He ran into serious foul trouble in the third quarter. Brown was whistled for his fourth foul with 9:53 left in the period for an off-arm shove on Aaron Nesmith. Wade entered and Brown exited.

The Sixers' slim lead didn't slip away. Walker nailed threes on consecutive possessions and Maxey jammed in a dunk.

Soon after, Tacko Fall came in for his first meaningful minutes as a Sixer. The 7-foot-6 two-way contract player grabbed an offensive board off a missed Edgecombe free throw, which drew one of the day's loudest cheers. With Fall on the floor, Maxey and James connected on an alley-oop that extended the Sixers' lead to 82-73.

When the Sixers tried to sit in a zone, Fall was called for a defensive three-second violation. Whatever the scheme, most of Fall's defensive work will come around the paint. He certainly has exceptional physical traits as a rim protector and is not nimble on the perimeter.

Fall logged five scoreless third-quarter minutes and recorded three rebounds. The Sixers outscored Indiana by a point with Fall on the court. Given Fall is occupying a (two-way) roster slot and the Sixers are so depleted at center, it made sense to see a bit of what he can do outside of garbage time. While five minutes isn't enough for any grand conclusions, it's very safe to say Fall is a unique player.

"I'm 7-6, so I can change the game in so many ways," Fall said. "Offensively, setting screens, making sure guys get open, being an easy target for lobs. Defensively, I feel like I've always been an elite rim protector and I've worked on my body a lot to be able to move a lot better."

Nurse praised Fall's outing, saying he "gave us some great minutes and a nice lift."

Fall is appreciative of his first NBA opportunity since the 2021-22 season.

"I've worked very hard," he said. "God has brought me back here and I'm thankful. And I'm ready. Whenever my name is called, I'm going to go out there and do my job."

The Sixers built their advantage to 102-87 with a Brown three early in the fourth quarter. They couldn't cruise to a blowout, though.

Siakam kept hurting the Sixers as a driver and had a highly efficient fourth quarter, scoring 19 points on 7-for-9 shooting. Quenton Jackson's layup trimmed Indiana's deficit to 119-115.

The Sixers ultimately held off the Pacers' push.

Caldwell-Pope canned a three, Wade threw down an and-one dunk, and James checked off his milestone assist with a late dish to Edgecombe for a layup.

#2676. 6 plays that cost the Cowboys vs. 49ers

46 points. The Dallas Cowboys defense, that we know isn't very good, allowed 46 points on 9.4 yards per play. How many times can you be disappointed before you're no longer surprised? At least just once more as we saw the defense surrender multiple big plays to San Francisco.

The offense made their mistakes as well, but it's hard not to focus on giving up nearly a 50-burger at home. You can pick so many plays to choose from as to why the Cowboys lost but perhaps it's easier to choose the ones that most irritated you in watching the Cowboys lose to the San Francisco 49ers yet again. Here are the plays that should get under your skin the most and why they matter in the grander scheme.

The Cowboys looked like they had wrestled the early momentum back from San Francisco after a George Pickens score. It's not too many times the Cowboys have led by multiple scores this season and the defense has needed any possible large lead it could get.

Facing 3rd-and-8 with the 49ers on their own 26-yard line, the Dallas defense proved why. The Cowboys did a great job of putting initial pressure on Brock Purdy but he managed to scramble out of the pocket and found Christian McCaffrey as got behind the defense for a short pass from Purdy. From there he went untouched for a 74-yard score.

For a moment you felt that the Cowboys could put the pressure on the 49ers for a change but boy would that be an ominous sign of things to come.

The theme of today was one explosive play after another. If there's one thing you expect from a Kyle Shanahan offense is misdirection and out-leveraging the defense for an advantage. Deebo Samuel historically has been a thorn in the side of the Cowboys, and once again he stuck the Cowboys right where it hurts.

Samuel took a reverse pitch from Kaelon Black and raced 70 yards down the sideline for a touchdown. When you watch the replay, notice how long it takes for the defense to process what is happening. Samuel has a convoy of blockers out in front while the majority of the Cowboys defense is on the other side of the field.

What are some of the basic principles of defense at at any level let alone the NFL? Defensive pursuit and perimeter containment. That's where the Cowboys tend to struggle mightily an Samuel made them pay. One missed assignment or poor angle against a player like Samuel can turn an ordinary running play into an instant touchdown.

The Cowboys avoided letting the 49ers score points at the end of the first half before they received the second half kickoff. Down by a one point, letting the 49ers score a touchdown would be detrimental. Unfortunately, Dallas could not prevent that from happening and rookie running back Kaelon Black ran all over the defense to make a point.

The play puts another red-hot spotlight on Caleb Downs. The rookie safety was run over by Black on a touchdown that helped San Francisco seize control of the second half. Downs also had trouble finishing plays in space, including a missed opportunity to contain Purdy before the quarterback found McCaffrey for a long touchdown.

For a player with his expectations, the Cowboys need more consistency, particularly against offenses that force defenders to make decisions in space. We need to see better from Downs down the stretch.

This is where the wheels started to fall off. Sure Brandon Aubrey made two kicks beyond 50 yards. However, Aubrey hasn't been as automatic anymore and now you sometimes have to hold you breath if he can make the routine kicks.

With Cowboys looking to take seven-point lead, Aubrey missed the extra point. This left the Cowboys chasing points for the remainder of the game. With the game going the way that it did, any points at all were needed. Dallas had an unsuccessful two-point try in an effort to make up the difference after Aubrey's miss.

Aubrey has also had kickoff penalties this year and onside kick attempt at the end of the game wasn't nearly good enough. There's something off with Aubrey, and whatever it is, it is hurting the Cowboys.

For all intents and purposes, this was the last straw. The Cowboys fought tirelessly to get back in the game but fell short on defense. After Prescott connected with Ryan Flournoy for an 11-yard touchdown on fourth down, Dallas had reduced San Francisco's lead to 38-32 with 3:42 remaining. The Cowboys needed one defensive stop to give Prescott a chance to win.

Instead, just 10 seconds of game clock later, Purdy found McCaffrey for a 66-yard touchdown on second-and-10. San Francisco added a two-point conversion, extending its lead to 46-32. This was arguably the most decisive moment of the game. Dallas had finally pulled within one possession, only for the defense to surrender another enormous touchdown immediately.

After the Cowboys drew the score to 40-46, it was longshot that the Cowboys could get the ball back with enough time to take the late lead. Quinnen Williams who has been one of the few bright spots for the Cowboys defense almost came up huge.

Looking to drain the remaining time off the clock, the 49ers handed the ball of to Kaelon Black. Williams darted through the 49ers offensive line to meet Black in the hole. Williams was able to dislodge the ball from Black's arms. The Cowboys had a chance to recover the ball before Black quickly regained possession for the 49ers.

If the defense can't be average, the least it can be is opportunistic and Williams almost gave that much when the team needed it badly. The Cowboys scored 40 points and still found a way to lose. That's the frustrating reality of this team. Dak Prescott threw five touchdowns, George Pickens delivered three scores, and Quinnen Williams nearly gave Dallas one final opportunity to steal a victory.

Yet none of it mattered because the defense couldn't stop San Francisco from producing one explosive play after another. At some point, these breakdowns stop being isolated mistakes and become the identity of your football team. For Dallas, that point may have already arrived.

#2675. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2672. Sixers, Brown have a ‘humbling' night in loss to Celtics

Sixers, Brown have a 'humbling' night in loss to Celtics originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Whatever Jaylen Brown and the Sixers dreamed up for their first matchup against the Celtics soon flew out the window on Tuesday night.

Brown was whistled for two early fouls, the Sixers fell behind and their early-season flaws were on full display in a 123-101 loss at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

"We've just got to get better," Brown said. "Tonight was humbling. We got outplayed, out-executed. So we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the next one."

Over 26 minutes, Brown had 13 points on 4-for-9 shooting and five rebounds against the team that traded him away this summer.

As for the endless dissection of his relationship with former co-star Jayson Tatum, Brown didn't have much to add Tuesday. There was no public reconciliation, no obvious on-court animosity and generally nothing to satisfy fans hoping for some kind of fireworks on that front.

"I'm just focused on doing what's best for my team," Brown said. "Everything else … to be honest, I wasn't paying attention. But credit to Jayson; he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics. They executed, they shot the hell out of the ball and they were the better team tonight."

Tatum scored 21 points, two of which came on a third-quarter slam over LeBron James. Paul George continued his fantastic start as a Celtic by dropping 36 points and draining six three-pointers.

The Celtics dominated from beyond the arc, shooting 22 for 49 (44.9 percent). The Sixers went just 11 for 37 (29.7 percent) on another night of underwhelming offense. The team sits 22nd in the NBA in offensive rating, 24th in three-point makes per game and 21st in three-point percentage.

"I think that we've got some guys that are obviously shooting much lower percentages than their last season or their career average — almost a handful of guys," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "And I don't think it's because they're shooting fallaway, totally contested ones. I think they're shots we want them to take. So I think they'll continue to take 'em and I'm pretty sure those will even out into their career averages."

Joel Embiid is at 37 percent from the floor and 4 for 33 from three-point range (12.1 percent).

The Sixers' seven-time All-Star center got through an injury scare when he rolled his ankle late in the second quarter and hit a three early in the third. It was his first long-range make since the Sixers' home opener back on Oct. 22.

"It's a work in progress," Embiid said. "I think the biggest thing is just not thinking. I'm probably overthinking it. The rhythm of the game is different. I'm so used to having to create for myself, so it's a little bit different.

"But I think I'm slowly getting better. You could see as soon as I made a three, the next shot in the short corner … I didn't even think about it. I just shot it and let it fly, and I made it. … I think it's just about taking what's in front of you. Make or miss, keep working on your game. It's going to get there at some point."

Even with the Sixers second in the Eastern Conference standings at 9-3, Embiid believes the team's defense has "slacked off a little bit" in recent games.

"I don't really look at the record," he said. "I just look at the process of, 'Are we getting better every day?' We can always do a better job at all phases of the game."

"They're one of the top teams in the league and they've been together for a while," Brown said. "We've got a lot to work on over here, so we've got to get to work."

The Sixers will face the Raptors on Thursday night in Philadelphia.

They'll have to wait until Jan. 21 in Boston to see the Celtics again.

"I was looking forward to this," Brown said. "I was looking forward to playing well, but s— happens. Just get ready for the next one."

#2671. NFC West Recap: 49ers hang 46 on Dallas; Rams rout Cardinals, Seahawks win

The San Francisco 49ers put up the most points and yards in franchise history for a road game, which is also the most yards the Dallas Cowboys have given up at home.

I'm just getting started on stats. We'll begin with the 49ers averaging 9.4 yards per play. That do anything for you? How about Brock Purdy going 22-of-28 for 389 yards passing and three touchdowns, finishing with a passer rating of 154.5. Then there's running back Christian McCaffrey, who had 223 yards from scrimmage and three scores.

And yet, they still, STILL had to recover an onside kick to win the game.

Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott threw five touchdown passes, while cornerback Deommodore Lenoir spent most of the afternoon chasing Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens. Renardo Green left with the same back injury he dealt with all week. There hasn't been much about Green's status for next week as of this writing, but Kyle Shanahan said he was already playing hurt.

It was 38-32 in the fourth quarter. All points were by the offense. No sacks (well, there was one, but I wouldn't call it "legitimate" outside of the stat sheet), and the Cowboys were coming back. Then this happened:

And even then, this thing wasn't over until the most entertaining fumbleroosky play in recent memory as the clock ticked to zero:

Regardless of whether we want to be optimistic or skeptical, the 49ers stay the NFC's No. 1 seed, a game ahead of the 7-2 pack of the Detroit Lions, Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears. The Seahawks and Rams both won, so the division lead stays at 2.5 games. The 49ers face a tough gauntlet, starting with the Vikings. Any questions you have about this team are about to be answered over the next four games.

After trading quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Vikings on Tuesday, the Las Vegas Raiders gave Fernando Mendoza his first NFL start. At first it looked like an upset, but then the Seahawks had to spoil the party.

There were moments, however. On Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock's first dropback, he tried to shovel the ball away to avoid a sack and fumbled. Mendoza scored on a quarterback draw a few plays later, and the Raiders led 10-7 at halftime. The second half belonged to the Seahawks, with highlights like rookie running back Jadarian Price scoring his first career touchdown to take the lead, and a 71-yard Jaxon Smith-Njigba score.

Final: 21-13. Smith-Njigba had 144 of his 171 yards receiving in the third quarter alone. Just like against the 49ers last week, the Raiders had a terrible second half with negative yards until their final possession. Mendoza took six sacks as well. The score could have been worse. Lock lost a second fumble when Zach Charbonnet ran into him on a play-action fake, and Jason Myers missed a 44-yarder. Right tackle Abe Lucas left with an ankle injury, which is worth watching before Seattle comes to Levi's Stadium in Week 12.

It was a lot of Seattle things, and then a lot of Raider-ing. Unfortunately, Seattle things usually don't end in losses the way Raider-ing does.

Minshew Magic is gone to IR. That led us to Carson Beck starting for Arizona. A rookie, Carson Beck.

So what happens? The Cardinals tried doing what worked last time they played the Rams: field-goal-ing them to death. This time, it wasn't as successful, as they managed only six points throughout the game. Besides Matthew Stafford's early-game interception to linebacker Cody Simon, it was all Los Angeles. Beck threw an interception just before halftime, and the Rams turned it into a 17-6 lead at the break.

Final: 34-6 in Glendale, the Rams' fourth straight win. Arizona finished with 123 yards of total offense: 89 net passing and 34 rushing. Beck was sacked five times, 1.5 of them by Aaron Donald. Stafford threw three touchdown passes. The Cardinals need to get through 2026 and make a football team next year.

Credit where it's due: the Rams look like a team again. They're 1-2 in the division, and their bye week comes before a Thanksgiving Eve game against the Packers. No credit is given to them for getting a team like the Cardinals, a team that beat them solely on field goals a few weeks back. Luckily, the Rams also have a tough stretch coming up: the Green Bay Packers and the Kansas City Chiefs.

The 49ers "host" the Minnesota Vikings (7-2) at Estadio Banorte in Mexico City on Sunday Night Football. The Vikings traded a 2027 third-round pick for Cousins, and he went 21-of-31 for 207 yards passing and two touchdowns in a 30-10 win at Lambeau. So they got the offense figured out; what about the defense? Well, they sacked Jordan Love eight times.

Just a reminder, that's not the Cowboys defense: Dallas sacked Purdy five times, and the 49ers still scored 46. This time the 49ers' defense has to carry its share. The No. 1 seed is on the line, and Minnesota won the last two meetings. Cousins also became the first quarterback since at least 1950 to start for two different teams in consecutive weeks, and last week's start was against the 49ers, when Jaden Dugger returned his pass for a touchdown. At least the game isn't in Minnesota.

The Rams and Seahawks are on bye. So, bye.

The Cardinals visit the Kansas City Chiefs, who beat Atlanta 35-13 behind five Patrick Mahomes touchdown passes. Gotta love it when the 49ers get Atlanta's best, but then they go back to doing Falcons things.

#2670. Drake Maye could be out for the rest of the season due to leg injury

Drake Maye could be out for the rest of the NFL season.

The New England Patriots quarterback is benched indefinitely after suffering a significant lower-leg injury during the Week 10 matchup against the Detroit Lions, played in Munich, Germany on Sunday, Nov. 15. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, the Patriots are currently concerned about an ankle fracture.

On the morning of Monday, Nov. 16, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel reported that Maye stayed in Germany out of an abundance of caution, with ESPN reporting that the quarterback is undergoing additional tests to see if he needs surgery.

During the final offensive snap in the opening drive against the Lions, Maye was sacked by pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson, with Maye's ankle getting caught under Hutchinson's.

Maye limped off to the locker room and did not return to the game.

With Maye sidelined, the Patriots' top backup quarterback choice is Tommy Devito, who stepped in against Detroit after Maye was injured. 28-year-old Devito has been with the Patriots for the past two seasons and became the primary backup to Maye entering 2026.

"My comfort level with Tommy is that I think he can help us if he has to play. He is prepared," Mike Vrabel told WEEI, New England's Sports Radio, on Monday, Nov. 16.

This article originally appeared on The Providence Journal: Drake Maye could be out for the rest of the season due to leg injury

#2668. 5 Bears Takes: Grading The First Half and Dissecting The NFC North

Following a fast and furious nine games, the Chicago Bears enjoyed their bye over the weekend. In the process, they watched two divisional foes beat each other up and got a live look at their Week 11 opponent as the Panthers beat them at home. The playoff picture continues to take shape, and the Bears will start practice early next week as they gear up for a second-half run. We'll cover all of that, and more in a special installment of 5 Bears Takes.

1. Grading out the offense over the first nine games of the season.

Before the season, head coach Ben Johnson spoke about wanting to set the NFL's scoring record. While some took those words and ran with them, the Bears were well on pace after a Week 1 that produced 59 points on the road. Since that point, the offense has yet to break the 40-point mark again, but they've eclipsed the 30-point mark four separate times. All of which were with starting quarterback Caleb Williams under center.

Through nine games, the offense ranks within the Top 5 in yards per game (383), Top 10 in points per game (26.8), 11th in EPA/play, and 10th in success rate. In total, their numbers are right around where they sat for the majority of last season, with one major caveat: They missed their starting quarterback for a third of the season (so far). They've also faced four of the Top 10 defenses in the league through that stretch.

Overall, there's still plenty of meat left on the bone when looking at this unit's production and what it could (or should) be. With better health at the quarterback position and no clunkers in the second half of the season, the Bears have a real opportunity to finish as a Top 5 offense. Part of that will depend on health at key positions like running back and receiver, but the offensive line will play a key part, too. We've seen multiple flashes of dominance, but there's still plenty to clean up, especially when it comes to penalties and self-inflicted mistakes. With a better-than-expected defense, they've been able to control most games, but for them to take the next step and be scarier down the stretch, the offense must be more consistent.

2. Grading out the defense over the first nine games of the season.

Coming into the season, the defense felt like the Achilles' heel of what could be a Super Bowl contender. During the offseason, the front office did very little to improve the defensive line, and through the first month and a half of the season, it seemed clear the interior defensive line wouldn't be good enough. Despite what their depth chart has looked like on paper, they've performed better than expected, even before the acquisition of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.

Through nine games, the defense ranks 1st in third-down percentage (22.8%), Top 5 in fourth-down percentage (30.8%), Top 10 in EPA/play, yards per game, and sacks, and gives up just 20.4 points per game. It's also worth mentioning that they were 9th in pressure percentage coming into Week 10. With Simmons in the mix on the interior, the biggest hole this group has is at cornerback. The hope is that with a healthy Malik Muhammad, either Jaylon Johnson or Tyrique Stevenson can step into the spot opposite the rookie and provide consistency and stability. With any luck, they'll get Coby Bryant back at some point in December. It's worth pointing out how well Cam Lewis has played since taking over the starting spot opposite first-round rookie Dillon Thieneman.

With the divisional defenses starting to shake out, this group must continue its upward trajectory. Getting back Dayo Odeyingbo should help the defensive line, but Austin Booker, Montez Sweat, and even Grady Jarrett have been noticeably better since the arrival of Simmons. Many expected the Bears to make another move or two before the deadline, but with nothing materializing, they're stuck with what they have. Similar to the offense, health will be key down the stretch, but overall, the team should feel pretty good about where they stand. The only real concern heading into the second half is how well their cornerbacks can perform against top offenses.

3. Dissecting the NFC North after another hectic week that saw the Bears drop from first to third place.

With the Bears' bye week, they were the only team in the division that was not in play on Sunday. The Detroit Lions took their crack at the piñata that has become the New England Patriots in the early-morning slot, and outside of the opening drive, it wasn't much of a game. The Patriots lost quarterback Drake Maye early, and, to put it nicely, backup quarterback Tommy DeVito was ineffective. For as impressive as the Lions were, they lost another star defender when Aidan Hutchinson went down with what appeared to be a serious knee injury following a sack of Maye on the first drive. The play (and subsequent celebration) took two of the most impactful players out of the game before it could really even get going. Although the Lions have been playing much better defense as of late, losing their top two leaders, Jack Campbell and Hutchinson, will wear on them as the season goes on.

During the next time slot, the Packers hosted the Kirk Cousins-led Vikings. What looked like a good matchup on paper turned into a season sweep for Minnesota, following a 30-10 drubbing. The Vikings' defense continues to be one of the best overall units in the league, and with Cousins under center, the offense looked more cohesive, even if it wasn't a perfectly played game. Cousins has plenty of familiarity with the offense, so it's fair to assume that he'll continue to hit the ground running. For the Packers, it's hard to know whether Sunday's 20-point loss was simply a bad day at the office, or a sign of things to come. Green Bay has shown clear holes all season, and although they've looked considerably better over the last month, there are still ways to attack them.

All in all, the division once again had another winning week. With the Lions and Vikings both winning, there's a three-way tie at the top with all three teams sitting at 7-2. The Packers will go on an abbreviated bye week before going to Los Angeles to face a red-hot Rams team on Thanksgiving Eve. Ultimately, their bye week will amount to the same number of days off as it would if they played on Thursday night and then played a Monday night game the following week.

It's clear that all four teams are playoff-caliber, but it remains to be seen if all four can make the playoffs come January. With Sunday's results, the Packers have now fallen a game and a half behind everyone else, while sporting a 1-3 record within the division. Even more troubling is that their 4-4 conference record won't help them much in tie-breakers once more games are played. Heading into Week 11, all four teams fill out the seven teams that would comprise the NFC playoff picture, but with plenty of head-to-heads remaining (both in the division and the conference), this is still a long way from a resolution.

Heading into Week 11, here's how the divisional standings look:

Lions win the head-to-head tie-breaker against the Vikings and have a better divisional record than the Bears.

Vikings win the head-to-head tie-breaker against the Bears.

After Week 11, each team will have seven games remaining. Both the Bears and Lions have favorable matchups, while the Vikings will play the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday Night Football. Barring a surprise, the Packers will find themselves a full two games back of first place. It's just a matter of how many teams will be sitting at 8-2 by the conclusion of next Sunday. It's also worth noting that Green Bay and Minnesota have just two divisional games remaining, while Detroit has three, and Chicago still has four.

Taking it a step further, here's how the remaining strength of schedule plays out for all four teams in the division:

For a division with four of the Top 7 teams in the NFC, each team's remaining strength of schedule all rank within the Top 10. In other words, buckle up, because this race is far from done.

4. Taking a deeper dive into the NFL playoff picture: The AFC is taking shape, while the NFC is still a nine-team race.

As we turn the page on Week 10, the playoff picture is truly taking shape in both conferences. The elite teams seem clear, as do the handful of teams that are all but out of the playoff picture. There aren't many middling teams in either conference, but there are more in the AFC than the NFC through 10 weeks. Taking a deeper dive into each conference, each race is becoming clear.

On the outside looking in: New England Patriots (5-5), Baltimore Ravens (4-5), Las Vegas Raiders (4-6)

The top of the AFC is loaded with top-tier teams. The Bills are tied with the 49ers for the best record in the league at (8-1) and have a favorable schedule down the stretch. In the AFC West, the Chiefs hold the tie-breaker over the Broncos, but with both games already in the books, it'll come down to whoever has the best divisional record. The loser of the West should take the fifth seed. The Jaguars and Bengals are both also sitting at 7-2, and an argument could be made for either team being right up there with the Bills. Barring a surprise with Jacoby Brissett under center, the AFC North looks like a two-team race, with the loser grabbing the sixth seed. The seventh seed will likely come down to the Browns and Patriots, but the Ravens have an outside shot if they can field a better offense. A few weeks ago, I would have taken the Patriots to earn that final Wild Card spot, but with their injuries and how bad they have played over their last two games, it feels like a true toss-up between the two. The Browns are a younger team and maybe aren't as talented as the Patriots, but sometimes the season's context matters. Houston's loss on Sunday against the Browns all but shut down their slim playoff hopes.

Flipping over to the NFC, it's a similar story, with a handful of clear "top teams." Yet, unlike the AFC, there's going to be a division winner (or two) who will finish with a worse record than most (if not all of) the Wild Card teams. While the 49ers currently hold the No. 1 seed, they'll see a handful of playoff-caliber teams over their final eight games. Here's a look at the current NFC playoff picture:

On the outside looking in: Seattle Seahawks (6-4), Los Angeles Rams (6-4), Dallas Cowboys (4-6)

While many had the 49ers as a potential playoff team, it's hard to imagine that anyone had them with a commanding two-game lead in a division with the defending Super Bowl Champions and this year's overwhelming Super Bowl favorites. Yet, here we are. Not only are the 49ers 8-1, but they are 3-0 within the division. Ultimately, they are likely to win most tie-breaking scenarios within the division, but they still have games against Minnesota, Kansas City, Seattle, and Los Angeles. The NFC North is a gauntlet, and that doesn't appear to change any time soon. There are still plenty of head-to-head matchups that will help shape the final standings, but for now the Lions hold the tie-breaker over both Minnesota and Chicago due to their divisional record (and head-to-head). I'm still not convinced all four will make the playoffs, but right now it seems like a good bet they'll send at least three. The Packers vs. Rams on Thanksgiving Eve will be big for tie-breaking purposes, as both teams come off bye weeks. The NFC East and NFC South are both disasters. We'll see if the Giants can maintain a record above .500, but the winner of the South seems less likely to hold that honor. Ultimately, the last three playoff spots will come from the North and West. The Cowboys have an outside chance, but at this point, that's likely more a divisional conversation than anything to do with the Wild Card.

Barring some great surprises, it could be argued that at least 10 of the 14 playoff teams are already "set". We'll see how the back end of each Wild Card race settles, but outside of that, the NFC South is the only division that is really up for grabs and could add or subtract someone from the overall playoff picture.

5. A second-half look ahead: With eight games remaining, what's the magic number to not only make the playoffs but secure a second consecutive NFC North title?

As highlighted above, the Bears head into their final eight games of the season with the hardest remaining schedule in the league based on current records. For reference, the .630 winning percentage is almost .200 points higher than the winning percentage they have faced in their current schedule. It's also worth mentioning that this includes a three-win Saints team on Sunday and a one-win Dolphins team in Week 14.

At 7-2, Chicago's current playoff probability sits in the high 80s, according to The Athletic and ESPN. They hold a game and a half lead on the trio of the Packers, Rams, and Seahawks, while already holding the head-to-head tiebreaker over Seattle.

Ultimately, 11 wins should get the Bears into the playoffs, but it's highly unlikely they'll outright win the division like they did last year. While they sit at 5-2 in the conference right now, their only two losses have come within the division. To make matters worse, they are the only team in the NFC North without a divisional win, after losses to the Vikings in Week 1 and the Packers in Week 5. The good news is that they still have four divisional games remaining. The bad news is that three of the four matchups will come over the final three games of the season.

Assuming they take care of business and beat the only two teams currently under .500 that they'll play, that would leave them at nine wins. Add in two divisional wins, and that leaves them at 2-4 within the division. Thus, the chances of 11 wins being enough to earn another NFC North title seem highly unlikely.

Finishing at 11-6 would mean a 4-4 finish, which in the grand scheme of things wouldn't be a terrible finish considering their strength of schedule. Matching their win total from a season ago with a harder schedule could be seen as a win, but it would also likely lock them into a Wild Card spot. While some look at potential matchups as the fifth or sixth seed and see the winners of the NFC East and NFC South, that's just one round of the playoffs. Having to win three games on the road to get to the Super Bowl is not impossible, but it's highly unlikely.

It's clear that the Bears are one of the better teams in football, but their remaining schedule will make it hard to finish with the type of record that will ultimately reflect how good they are as a team. With that being said, a 3-1 finish in the division, coupled with winning against the Saints and Dolphins, might be good enough to get the job done.

Here's how the schedule looks over the final eight games of the season starting Sunday:

While 4-4 would be "acceptable," the baseline over their final eight games should be a 5-3 record. Sure, it won't be easy, but 2-0 against below .500 teams and 3-1 in the division would get it done. If they go 2-2 within the division, a split between AFC juggernauts could also make sense. The Bears likely won't be favored in all of their games, but that doesn't mean they won't have more than a fighting chance in each one. Some matchups are more favorable than others, but as we've learned with this team so far in 2026, they can beat anyone. 12-5 might be enough to win the division, but a 13-4 record might be good enough to not only lock down the North but also push them into the No. 1 seed, depending on how San Francisco looks down the stretch.

Overall, it's safe to say that six out of the final eight games will have a playoff-like atmosphere, and although they'll only have three standalone games in this stretch, I would not be surprised to see the Jaguars or Lions game flexed before Week 18. No matter how it shakes out, this team is in great shape not only for the division, but also to be primed for a Super Bowl run. They'll have plenty of stiff competition in front of them, which will help once January rolls around. Embrace the difficulty, and just know that most of these games will feel like standalone playoff games over the next eight weeks.

#2667. Report: Premier League keeper ticks a number of boxes to replace Alisson

Bart Verbruggen would make sense as a potential Liverpool goalkeeper signing, according to David Lynch, who has revealed the club previously held regular contact with his agent.

Speaking on Anfield Index's Media Matters podcast, Lynch described the Brighton goalkeeper as an option with several attractive qualities as Liverpool consider their longer-term plans.

However, he did not report an active negotiation or suggest that Alisson Becker's departure had been decided. His assessment was that Liverpool face connected decisions over their current goalkeepers and the identity of a potential successor.

Lynch's most concrete information concerned Liverpool's interest before Verbruggen joined Brighton.

"I know that they had watched him. They spoke to his agent quite regularly prior to him moving to Brighton," he said.

"So there's a long-term interest in there."

That history helps explain why the Dutch goalkeeper could feature in future discussions. It does not establish that Liverpool have renewed those conversations or made an approach.

Lynch nevertheless considered the profile appealing.

"He feels a better fit. He's Premier League ready," he said.

"It just ticks so many boxes. It just makes you think that would be very Liverpool to do that deal, to be honest."

He also cited a potentially favourable contract situation as part of the appeal. No proposed fee, offer or agreement was identified during the discussion.

Lynch acknowledged that retaining Alisson remains an option, particularly because the succession plan is not straightforward.

Liverpool must consider what the goalkeeper can still offer alongside his fitness record and the terms required to persuade him to extend.

Lynch raised a hypothetical example in which Liverpool might prefer a shorter agreement while another club offered greater security. He was illustrating a negotiating difficulty, not reporting a competing offer.

"It's not as easy as to say, 'Well, we want to keep Alisson for at least another year. Let's give him another deal.' He can push back on that himself as well," he said.

That makes the decision mutual. Liverpool's preference alone would not settle the situation, even if they concluded that another season together was the best immediate outcome.

Giorgi Mamardashvili's readiness to take over is another central consideration.

Lynch recognised improvement in his performances but remained concerned about his work in possession.

"I think he's done a little better this season, made some good saves," he said.

"But that distribution is just such a black mark against him, I would say, in terms of him being a Liverpool goalkeeper."

The issue, in Lynch's assessment, is how Liverpool use the position. A goalkeeper must contribute to progressing possession as well as preventing goals.

"You have to do more than that when you're the Liverpool goalkeeper," he said.

"You are going to have to break lines with your passing or at least look a little bit more comfortable than he does."

Lynch did not dismiss the possibility of improvement, noting that Mamardashvili remains young for his position. His concern was whether Liverpool would consider him ready to become first choice now.

With Lucca Brughmans also still developing, Liverpool have several possible routes rather than one obvious answer.

They could retain Alisson, promote Mamardashvili or look outside the club. Verbruggen's previous connection and Premier League experience explain why Lynch regards him as worth watching.

The larger point is that deciding to move on from a senior player is only half the task.

"You don't have to just make a good decision around Alisson, which might be to let him go," Lynch said.

"You have to make a really good decision next in terms of who succeeds."

That is why Lynch's verdict remained cautious despite his enthusiasm for Verbruggen's suitability. Liverpool need a convincing succession plan, and the transcript establishes neither a final decision nor an imminent signing.

#2664. Packers must go back to the drawing board on the offensive line

No quarterback — even one who has been playing at an MVP level of late — can sustain an offense when he can't get the ball out of his hands. Jordan Love is no exception, and Green Bay Packers fans saw the team's fatal flaw get exploited over and over and over again on Sunday afternoon.

The Minnesota Vikings defense is a singularly bad matchup for the Packers, who continue to make inexplicable decisions with their personnel on the offensive line. Yes, the team has had a glut of injuries up front, and third-string center John Williams was one of the biggest problems on the line on Sunday, but every single player shared in the blame for the constant and, even more problematic, instant pressure that Love faced all game long.

Love couldn't even get the ball out quickly without players in his face, let alone try to dial up any deep balls, which have been a staple of the team's recent success. So what is there to do?

Is the answer just as simple as "don't play the Vikings again"? Are there answers on this roster, perhaps on injured reserve (looking at you, Sean Rhyan), who could help get this unit back on track? Maybe this team needs to get back to the drawing board at a more fundamental level when it comes to the offensive line — starting with the position coach and working all the way up.

The Packers have a long week to start working on some answers before their next game, which is a week from Wednesday in Los Angeles. They've got seven more chances to sort things out and find a way into the postseason. It's time to get this under control

#2662. How NFC North rivals did during Bears’ Week 10 bye

The Chicago Bears were idle in Week 10 due to their bye. At 7-2, they entered their bye week first in the NFC North, which is on track to become the greatest division in NFL history. It is the first time in league history that all four teams in a division were three or more games over .500 after Week 9.

The other three teams, the Detroit Lions, Green Bay Packers, and Minnesota Vikings, were all in action, however, while the Bears had the week off. Detroit played against the New England Patriots in Germany to kick off the Sunday slate, while the Packers and Vikings played each other in a key divisional showdown.

Here's a look at how the NFC North fared in Week 10 and the current standings, which remain deadlocked heading into Week 11.

Early in the Germany game, the Lions knocked out Patriots quarterback Drake Maye with an injury. That was the beginning of a disaster for the Patriots, as the Lions ended up winning the game 35-10. That's the second week in a row that an NFC North rival obliterated New England, much to the dismay of the Bears. It was a costly win for the Lions, however, as they lost superstar defensive end Aidan Hutchinson to injury. He injured his knee celebrating a sack in the first quarter, and he did not return. The Lions fear the worst, which would be the type of knee injury that cancels the rest of his season and potentially the beginning of next season.

From the opening kickoff to the final whistle, the Vikings had their way with the Packers. They beat them in every facet of the game, and the 30-10 final score brought the Vikings to 7-2 and dropped the Packers to 6-4. This was the first game back with the Vikings for quarterback Kirk Cousins. He was traded back to the Vikings after a few years away ahead of the trade deadline, and the early returns are good for them. He went 21/31 for 207 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception. He isn't a superstar, but he knows how to win football games, especially with a good roster like the Vikings have.

Now, the Bears Vikings, and Lions are all tied at the top of the division with a 7-2 record. Detroit has a win over Minnesota, and the Vikings have a win over the Bears, so that is the order of the tiebreaker at this time. Chicago still has one more game against Minnesota and two against Detroit remaining on the schedule. Even the last-place Packers, at 6-4, are a threat. They have a win against the Bears as well, but it was without Caleb Williams, as he was still working his way back from an injury. No matter what, they are a hurdle for every team in the division until they are no longer playing this season.

Did this bye week go how the Bears would have liked? No. In a perfect world for them, the Patriots would have won, and you can argue that the Packers beating the Vikings would have been better. However, seeing Green Bay with two more in the loss column may not be the worst thing, as overcoming the Vikings and Lions may be easier mentally for the Bears. There is a chance that all four of these teams make it to the postseason. Is it likely? No. But they are all dominating every game they play against non-divisional opponents. When they play each other, however, someone has to lose.

Next up for the Bears is a Week 11 matchup against the New Orleans Saints. The Lions will play the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Vikings will play the San Francisco 49ers, and the Packers will be on a bye. However, Green Bay's bye will be short-lived, as they have a Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Los Angeles Rams. Chicago, based on opponent winning percentage, has the hardest schedule remaining of any team in the NFL. Part of that is because of their divisional strength. Non-conference opponents include Super Bowl contenders like the Buffalo Bills and Jacksonville Jaguars too, so there is nothing easy about the final eight games. With that said, the Bears are an elite team that controls their own destiny.

#2661. Celtics’ historic start against Mavericks proved plenty: ‘We got a really, really good team’

BOSTON — The Dallas Mavericks stood no chance coming into TD Garden on Sunday night. It only took the Boston Celtics 12 minutes to make that abundantly clear.

The Celtics outscored the Mavericks 42-9 in the first quarter. No, that's not a typo. It was the largest first-quarter point differential in franchise history and the biggest margin in a single quarter since the Los Angeles Lakers outscored the Sacramento Kings 40-4 in 1987.

"We got a really, really good team," Jayson Tatum said after Boston's 131-94 win. "And I think it really just starts with our depth. Especially in that fourth, fifth spot of whoever we want to come in and start. Whether it's Hugo [González]. Whether it's Baylor [Scheierman]. Whether it's J-Walsh. Ron [Harper Jr.], all those guys are interchangeable, more than capable."

Dallas entered on the second night of back-to-back, without Kyrie Irving, and coming off brutal consecutive road losses to the Minnesota Timberwolves and Cleveland Cavaliers — in which they allowed an average of 130 points, the most they've allowed back-to-back this season.

Boston entered riding a five-game winning streak with the best record in the Eastern Conference, fresh off three days' rest and with a squeaky-clean injury report.

From the jump, the difference between the two teams that crossed paths in the NBA Finals just two years ago became glaringly apparent.

The Celtics made 16 of their first 27 shots, including seven of their first 13 threes. The Mavericks, ice-cold as soon as they came out of the players' tunnel, opened the game 2-for-18, missing all eight of their 3-point attempts. From there, nothing changed.

At least nothing significant enough to turn the tide.

Dallas found somewhat of a rhythm from long range, knocking down five 3-pointers in the second quarter, then again in the third to cut Boston's lead down to 25 points, but that was as close as the Mavericks ever got to sniffing a competitive ballgame.

Nov 15, 2026; Boston, Massachusetts, USA; Waiting for play to start up during the second half against the Dallas Mavericks are (left to right) Boston Celtics guard Ron Harper Jr. (8), guard Hugo Gonzalez (28), guard Devin Carter (99), center Luka Garza (52) and guard Baylor Scheierman (55) at TD Garden. Mandatory Credit: Winslow Townson-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

For Boston, concerns about maintaining double-digit leads were a non-factor. Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla believes focusing on protecting a lead misses the bigger picture of what his team is truly honing in on.

"It's not about hanging onto leads," Mazzulla said. "That's a passive mindset. It's not about building on them. It's understanding the ebbs and flows of the game and constantly answering the questions: Are we playing well? Having a good process? Or are we not playing well? And that's something you learn over the course of the season."

Tatum was the only Celtic to play over 25 minutes, logging 30:08, giving Mazzulla plenty of leeway to unleash Boston's depth. González, Scheierman, Harper, Luka Garza and Devin Carter each played at least 12 minutes, combining to score 35 points off the bench.

Their ability to easily insert themselves into action remains a part of the team Mazzulla will never look past.

"They don't care about who starts, who finishes, 10 minutes, 24 minutes," Mazzulla said. "They just impact winning. They're not distracted by any nonsense, and they understand that any night they can do something different that gives us a chance to win — whether it's guarding the other team's best player, whether it's rebounding, whether it's crashing on the offensive glass. Those guys take pride in having a role on our team that's necessary to get to where we wanna get to."

In the closing seconds of the fourth quarter, with Boston's lead hovering around 40 points, Scheierman dove headfirst toward a loose ball that eventually went out of bounds. Mazzulla and the rest of the Celtics' bench immediately rushed over to help him up.

That best reflected the standard Mazzulla and his coaching staff expect from this group, playing until the final buzzer regardless of the score rather than easing up when the outcome appears decided.

Even Maine native Cooper Flagg was impressed.

"Just the level that they were competing at," Flagg said. "You know, something that we need to look at and look in the mirror and decide if we're competing at that same level. And if we want it as bad as they did, and I don't think we did."

Flagg continued his praise of Boston: "I feel like we weren't competing at a high enough level, and that's kind of been — over the last three games on this road trip — what it's been. So taking that from them. Just we gotta compete at a high enough level."

The Celtics checked just about every box on Sunday night:

Shoot 41.8 percent from 3-point range on 55 attempts: Check.

Build a double-digit lead and never relinquish it: Check.

Hold Flagg to 17 points on 33.3 percent shooting and a minus-30: Check.

Run Dallas into the ground and give the end of the bench some extended minutes: Check.

Limit every starter (besides Tatum) to fewer than 25 minutes: Check.

It was the most dominant version of this Celtics team we've seen all season.

Tatum's smiles in the locker room suggested he and his teammates know it: They've got something special brewing in Boston. That doesn't mean they'll score 130 points, hold an opponent to nine in a quarter and run teams into the ground every night.

The Bills put up 7.2 yards per play thanks to the contributions of Allen and Cook, but the defense did its part in limiting New York's scoring opportunities, especially in the red zone. Buffalo has now won five straight games after beating the Jets and now seem to be leading the AFC East by a wide margin after the Patriots lost earlier on Sunday in their international matchup.

Here is the stock report for the Bills following Sunday's win over New York:

Cook has been on a tear this season as he seems to have found his groove on the ground and the Bills have been more than willing to let him run the football as much as he can handle. Against the Jets, Cook made the most of his carries as he achieved his highest rushing average in a game this season and he did that by nearly two yards per carry.

#2654. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2651. Lions star Aidan Hutchinson reportedly sustains torn ACL while celebrating sack of Drake Maye

Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson made his presence known early against the New England Patriots. On the Patriots' first offensive drive, Hutchinson broke through the line on third down and sacked Drake Maye.

Following the play, Hutchinson got up to celebrate the sack. He jumped into the air and immediately fell to the ground after landing. Hutchinson appeared to be holding his right knee.

Reports Monday suggested Hutchinson tore his ACL during the celebration. He'll miss the rest of the season recovering from the injury.

Hutchinson was able to walk off the field, but headed straight to the medical tent on the sideline. He was later spotted on the broadcast heading to the locker room.

He was deemed questionable to return with a knee injury, but late in the third quarter, he was ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Detroit eventually cruised to a 35-10 victory.

Preliminary reporting Sunday hinted at a potentially "significant" knee injury for Hutchinson.

After the game, Lions head coach Dan Campbell said the team would get more information on Hutchinson's injury when it returned to the United States.

"We'll know more when we get back in the States," head coach Dan Campbell said postgame, according to the Detroit News' Nolan Bianchi. "Anytime you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is, he's a captain of ours, that doesn't make things easy."

Hutchinson wasn't the only player injured on the play. Maye also left the game. He was deemed questionable to return due to an ankle injury before eventually also being ruled out. Maye is also in danger of missing the rest of the season due to the injury.

Losing Hutchinson for any significant period of time would be a devastating result for the Lions. Coming into the game, Hutchinson was Pro Football Focus' top-graded edge rusher on the year.

While NFL players rarely get injured while celebrating plays, it has happened before. Famously in 2001, Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica tore his ACL after celebrating a first quarter field goal in a game against the New York Giants.

More recently for the Lions, in 2014 former linebacker Stephen Tulloch celebrated a sack of Aaron Rodgers and suffered a season-ending ACL injury.

#2649. Stock up, stock down following the Jets' loss to the BIlls

The New York Jets (2-8) had what looked to be their most frustrating game of the season last week when multiple players showed visible dismay with the product on the field thus far. New York doesn't seem to get a break from the schedule as they welcomed the Buffalo Bills (8-1) to MetLife Stadium, but the Jets weren't able to flip the script on how their season has gone to this point.

The Jets lost to the Bills 31-12 on Sunday in a game where New York trailed Buffalo just 10-6 heading into halftime, but the Bills were able to capitalize on their trips in the red zone. Jets quarterback Geno Smith, who dealt with multiple issues in this game, threw for just 148 yards before leaving the game due to an ankle injury while 2026 fourth-round pick Cade Klubnik had an uneven performance in replacement of Smith.

The Bills were just 2-of-10 on third down, but that didn't matter much as quarterback Josh Allen and company averaged 7.2 yards per play with running back James Cook carrying the ball 18 times for 157 yards and one touchdown. Ultimately, despite New York getting solid outings from running back Breece Hall and wide receiver Garrett Wilson, the Jets just couldn't keep up in this game offensively.

Here is the stock report for the Jets following Sunday's loss to the Bills:

Wilson was the overwhelming leader in targets in the passing game as Smith looked for him on virtually every play, which makes sense considering how good the young receiver is at getting open. This was one of Wilson's better games of the season as he caught seven of his 14 targets for 106 (15.1 yards per reception), showing off his ability to consistently make plays.

Sadiq was only targeted twice so it's fair to say that he wasn't given much of a chance to make plays against the Bills on Sunday, but that would be ignoring how much is to be expected of the first-round rookie. This was Sadiq's second time in the past four weeks with finishing a game with less than six receiving yards and for a guy of his talent, he has to provide more.

This was arguably Phillips' best game of the season as he was consistently making plays in the run defense aspect and almost half of his tackles came by his own effort. Phillips has been one of the players that the Jets were hoping could stuff the run and while he has been doing that for the most part, this game stood out with how active he was in run support.

While Bailey has already been having the kind of season that should make the Jets proud to have selected him with the second overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, this was arguably his worst game of the year. Bailey had just one tackle on the day, but even though he wasn't able to get to Allen much over the course of the game, he still batted down two balls at the line of scrimmage.

Hall made his return to the Jets last week and the team didn't hesitate to put him back into his normal role as the starting running back and Sunday's game against the Bills looked like he was back to his usual self. Hall carried the ball 11 times for 41 yards, but he also caught all four of his passes for 67 yards, showing his impact in the passing game when he gets going.

Coming into this game, the Jets had been around middle of the pack in terms of how efficient opposing teams were when they ran the football (4.1 yards per carry), but the Bills flipped that on its head Sunday. Cook himself ran for 157 yards on 8.7 yards per carry, but Buffalo as a team averaged 6.3 yards per rush and scored three of their four touchdowns on the ground.
